question: What will voter turnout be in Spain's November 29, 2026 general election?

calls.reasoning: Resolution counts CERA voters in the electorate (2023 official was 66.59%, vs 70.40% for residents only). CERA is now 2.77M (7.2% of 38.73M), with roughly 10% CERA turnout in 2023, so total ≈ 0.928*resident + 0.7pp. Resident turnout reference: 2015-2023 range 69.8-75.8, mean ~71.8; one 29N poll projects 68.4% for residents; a polarized snap November election (no summer penalty) argues somewhat higher. Median resident ~70.5 gives total ~66.1. Polymarket turnout brackets (thin, ~$14k; 70%+ at 38-45c, implied median ~69) probably resolve on the resident-only figure, so they are a near-miss that implies a total of about 64.5-65.5; I treat them as evidence, not an anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Election: snap general election 29 Nov 2026, called 5 Oct after Junts/PP/Vox defeated housing decrees; Cortes dissolved 6 Oct (BOE) (Wikipedia, Al Jazeera, Euronews, Oct 2026).
- Census (INE press release EG2026): 38,728,356 total electors; CERA (abroad) 2,769,645 = 7.2%, +444,335 vs 2023 (probably partly new citizens under the Ley de Memoria Democrática 'nietos' route).
- Resolution instrument: official turnout includes CERA in both numerator and denominator, i.e. the definitive Ministry/JEC figure, NOT the election-night resident-only figure. 2023: resident-only 70.40% vs official incl. CERA 66.59%. Nov 2019: ~69.9 vs 66.23. Apr 2019: ~75.75 vs 71.76.
- CERA turnout 2023: 233,688 voters = 10.04% of CERA census (Newtral, 28 Jul 2023), first general election after voto rogado was abolished (2022); highest since 2008.
- Arithmetic: total ≈ 0.928*resident turnout + 0.0715*CERA turnout. At CERA turnout 10%: resident 68 -> 63.8; 70.4 -> 66.0; 72 -> 67.5; 74 -> 69.4; 76 -> 71.3.
- Poll (Infobae, 27 Oct 2026): one survey projects resident turnout of 68.43% ('below the 71% of 2023'), with 50% abstention among 18-29 year-olds vs 29.7% among those over 64.
- Poll average Oct 2026: PP 32.0, PSOE 26.4, Vox 18.8, Sumar 6.0, Podemos 2.9; PP+Vox above 176 seats in most polls (Infobae/El Debate).
- Postal vote: requests open until 19 Nov, deposit deadline 25 Nov; Comunitat Valenciana ~15k requests by 1 Nov, described as 'soaring' (moncloa.com). No national total found.
- Context: housing protests, polarized campaign. November date avoids the July holiday effect of 2023; the Nov 2019 repeat election had low turnout from fatigue (66.23 incl. CERA).
- Base rates: over all 16 elections since 1977, official turnout mean ~71.7, range 66.2-80.0. Over 2015-2023 (5 elections): 66.23-71.76, mean 68.1. Resident-only 2015-2023: ~69.8-75.8.
- Status quo: a repeat of 2023 resident turnout (~70.4) with the larger CERA share gives ~66.0 official.
- Event window: single election day 29 Nov 2026; the figure used is the latest published by 31 Dec 2026 (the CERA count is added a few days after election night). As of 4 Nov, 0% elapsed (election in 25 days).
- Searched but not found: Polymarket's rule text on CERA inclusion; a national postal-vote request total; CIS turnout projection; turnout of new 'nietos' CERA voters.
calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections 2015-2023, turnout including CERA (69.67, 66.48, 71.76, 66.23, 66.59)

calls.reasoning: Total turnout ~= 0.928*resident-turnout + ~0.7 (CERA is 7.15% of the 38.73M census and votes at ~9-10%). Resident turnout ranged 69.8-75.8% in 2015-2023 and was 69.8-70.4% in the last three elections. Centring it at ~70.5% gives a total of ~66.2%. Upside: polarising housing crisis, possible change of government, multiple crises. Downside: late-November date, fatigue. Polymarket band markets (~$14.5k volume) imply a median of ~69%, but they probably resolve on the election-night figure that excludes CERA. After converting, they are consistent with ~65-66% on this question's basis, so I used them as evidence, not an anchor.
calls.dossier:
- INE press note (Oct 2026): 38,728,356 electors for 29-N 2026; 35,958,711 resident in Spain, 2,769,645 abroad (CERA, 7.15% of census); 1,615,127 first-time resident voters. Census up 3.4% vs 2023.
- Overseas voters can vote without the old voto rogado (prior application) requirement, abolished in 2022; 2023 was already under the no-application regime.
- 2023 CERA turnout: 233,688 votes, ~10% of 2.29M CERA (Newtral, 28 Jul 2023); the Junta Electoral Central (JEC) report gives 203,115 (8.9%).
- Total turnout (incl. CERA), per question background: 2015 69.67, 2016 66.48, Apr-2019 71.76, Nov-2019 66.23, 2023 66.59. Resident-only election-night figures (recall): 2015 ~73.2, 2016 ~69.8, Apr-2019 ~75.75, Nov-2019 ~69.9, 2023 ~70.4.
- Identity: total ~= (resident share 0.9285 x resident turnout) + (0.0715 x CERA turnout ~0.09-0.10). At resident turnouts of 68/70/72/74, total ~= 63.8/65.7/67.6/69.4.
- Context (Al Jazeera/CNN/Euronews, 5 Oct 2026): Sánchez called a snap election after PP, Vox and Junts defeated his housing decrees amid mass housing protests. Polls show a PP+Vox majority as the most likely outcome. Wikipedia also lists floods, wildfires, an Iran war, a Ceuta migrant crisis and corruption scandals as salient issues.
- CIS 45,000-interview pre-election survey (fieldwork 7 Oct-7 Nov) includes a 70%-turnout scenario; no explicit turnout forecast found.
- Late-November date: no Spanish general-election precedent except Nov 2011 (68.94 total, under the old CERA rules) and Nov 2019 (66.23, a repeat election with fatigue).
- Resolution instrument: resolves off the official total incl. CERA (Ministry of the Interior/JEC, latest figure as of 31 Dec), NOT the election-night resident-only figure, which runs ~3.5-4.5 pts higher. Betting markets on turnout bands may use the night figure.
- Event window: single election day, 29 Nov 2026; final figure latest as of 31 Dec 2026. As of 4 Nov 2026, the vote has not occurred.
- Searched but not found: published turnout projections for 2026; Polymarket resolution rules text.
calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections 2015-2023 (total turnout incl. CERA), adjusted for the growing CERA share after the 2022 abolition of the overseas-vote application requirement (voto rogado)

calls.reasoning: Resolves on the definitive CERA-inclusive figure (2023: 70.40% resident-only on election night vs 66.59% definitive). CERA is now 7.2% of the electorate (2.77M of 38.73M), up from ~6.2%, with low turnout (~9% in 2023), so the total is about 0.928*resident + ~0.65. Resident-turnout estimates for 29-N run from 67.6% to 74%; one poll gives 68.4%. Polarization over Vox possibly entering government argues for mobilization; a snap late-November vote argues against. Taking resident turnout at ~70.5% (SD ~2.5) gives a total median of ~66.1. Polymarket's ladder (~$14.5k volume) has 70%+ at 0.38-0.45 and 68-70% at ~0.29, an implied median of ~69-70%; its rules could not be read, but those prices only fit a resident-only figure, so it is used as evidence about resident turnout rather than as an anchor.
calls.dossier:
- Election: Sánchez called a snap general election for 29 Nov 2026 after Junts, PP and Vox defeated his housing decrees; Cortes dissolved 6 Oct 2026 (Wikipedia/Al Jazeera/Euronews, 5-6 Oct 2026). Polls show PP ahead in all 13 October polls, with PP+Vox at ~203 seats (Infobae, 27 Oct 2026); the main story is whether Vox enters government.
- Census (INE press note, Oct 2026): 38,728,356 electors in total, 35,958,711 resident (CER) and 2,769,645 abroad (CERA). CERA is 7.2% of the total, 444,335 more than in 2023; growth is driven partly by the 'ley de nietos'. Madrid's CERA rose 31.45%.
- CERA no longer needs voto rogado (abolished 2022); documentation is sent automatically. Postal voting runs until 24 Nov; consular urns 21-26 Nov.
- Instrument trap: the election-night provisional turnout EXCLUDES CERA. In 2023 it was 70.40% provisional vs 66.59% definitive including CERA (Newtral, 18 Sep 2023). The 2023 electorate was 37,469,458 with 24,952,447 votes cast; implied CERA turnout ~9%.
- Formula: total ≈ 0.928 × resident turnout + 0.072 × CERA turnout. With CERA at 8-11%, total ≈ resident − ~4.4 pts.
- Historical definitive (CERA-inclusive) turnout: 2011 68.94, 2015 69.67, 2016 66.48, Apr-2019 71.76, Nov-2019 66.23, 2023 66.59. Resident-only: Nov-2019 ~69.9, 2023 70.4, Apr-2019 ~75.8.
- Poll turnout estimates for 29-N (resident basis): one poll 68.43% (expects ~50% abstention among 18-29s); a survey aggregate implies 67.6%; a Demócrata analysis says 'points to 74%', the highest since 2004.
- CIS pre-electoral study 3584 has a 45,000-person sample; results not yet seen.
- Upward factors: polarization over a PP-Vox government (the 2019-April mobilization analog), housing protests. Downward factors: late-November snap election, youth abstention, new low-propensity CERA registrants.
- Resolves off the definitive CERA-inclusive figure (Interior Ministry / Junta Electoral Central), not the election-night provisional figure.
- Event window: election day 29 Nov 2026; the latest figure as of 31 Dec 2026 is used. As of 4 Nov 2026 the vote has not happened.
- Not found: Polymarket's exact rules on CERA inclusion; 2026 CERA turnout projections; CIS turnout estimate.
calls.reference_class: Spanish general elections 2011-2023, definitive CERA-inclusive turnout (68.94, 69.67, 66.48, 71.76, 66.23, 66.59), adjusted for CERA's growing share since the 2022 abolition of voto rogado

calls.reasoning: Resolves on the definitive figure that includes voters abroad (CERA). In 2023 that was 66.59%, against 70.40% for residents only on election night. CERA is now 2.77M of 38.73M electors (7.15%) and voted at roughly 9-10% in 2023, so total ≈ 0.928 × resident turnout + ~0.7. The reference class is resident turnout in 2015-2023: 69.8-75.8%, and 69.8-70.4% in the last three elections. For 29-N, polls put resident turnout at 68.4% and 67.6%; one analysis says 74%. Upward pressure: polarization over Vox possibly entering government and the housing protests. Downward pressure: a snap election in late November, youth abstention, and newly registered CERA voters who rarely vote. A resident median of ~70.5% gives a total of ~66.1%. The Polymarket band markets are thin (about $14.5k across the bands); 70%+ trades at 0.38, implying a median of ~69%. That price fits a resident-only basis, so I use it as evidence about resident turnout, not as an anchor. The basis could not be confirmed, so it adds slight upside risk.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: the CERA-inclusive definition, 2.77M CERA voters (7.15%), CERA turnout of ~9-10%, the 2023 figures of 70.40 resident-only vs 66.59 official, and polls of 67.6-74 for residents. The only open factual question is which figure the Polymarket bands resolve on. None of the runs could read the rules, and I have no web access to check. Its prices fit a resident-only basis (implying ~65.2 official), and Polymarket usually uses headline election-night figures. I therefore treat it as weak evidence, which slightly fattens the upper tail without moving the median. Where to centre resident turnout is a judgment call: November avoids the July holiday penalty and polarization is high, but this is a snap vote with low youth mobilization. The polls average about 70 for residents. I agree with the runs' ~70.5 for residents and carry their reference class and dispersion forward. I priced no escape mass beyond 55 or 80 because I see no mechanism for it.

disagreements.claim: Whether the Polymarket turnout bands resolve on the resident-only election-night figure or the CERA-inclusive one
disagreements.verdict: Unsettled: no run could read the rules and no web access here. Their prices fit resident-only best, so I treat them as evidence about resident turnout, with a small upside-tail allowance.

disagreements.claim: Where to centre 29-N resident turnout (polls 67.6-68.4 vs an analysis pointing to 74)
disagreements.verdict: Centred at ~70.5 resident, giving ~66.1 official. The polarization upside and the late-November/snap-vote downside roughly offset.

disagreements.claim: Width of the distribution (runs gave a 10-90 width of 6.0-6.8)
disagreements.verdict: 6.6, from a resident SD of ~2.7 scaled by the 0.928 resident share plus CERA uncertainty.
